translation: Target is the proposition that for every set K of arithmetic sentences and every arithmetic theory (set of arithmetic sentences) F, assuming that (1) F is recursively enumerable, (2) every theorem of 𝗜𝚺₁ is a theorem of F, and (3) every theorem of 𝗜𝚺₁ is a theorem of K, if (4) K is closed under first-order deduction (every arithmetic sentence derivable from K belongs to K), (5) K is consistent (does not prove a contradiction), and (6) K contains the full local reflection schema for F.craig—that is, for every arithmetic sentence σ, the sentence Prov_{F.craig}(⌜σ⌝) 🡒 σ belongs to K, where F.craig is the Δ₁-presented axiom set with the same theorems as F obtained via Craig's trick and Prov_{F.craig} is its standard provability predicate—then the set of all theorems of F is a strict subset of K (every theorem of F belongs to K, and not every element of K is a theorem of F). Neither K nor F is required to be true in the standard model, K is not required to be recursively enumerable, F is not explicitly assumed to be consistent, and F.theory ⊆ K is part of the conclusion rather than a hypothesis.

divergences.description: Because the formalization works in plain first-order arithmetic rather than epistemic arithmetic (EA or EA_T), there is no object-language knowledge operator K or truth predicate T; Lean cannot express the global soundness antecedent K(F ⊆ T), nested knowledge, or S4 epistemic axioms, and states a meta-level implication over sets of arithmetic sentences using the pointwise local reflection schema instead (a declared idealization that aligns with Koellner's weaker pointwise antecedent).

Target restricts F to recursively enumerable theories extending 𝗜𝚺₁ ([F.RE] and [𝗜𝚺₁ ⪯ F]), whereas the source passages quantify over any formal system or algorithm F (and Theorem 3 over any formula F(x)). Although acknowledged in the claim and harmless (any RE theory F not extending 𝗜𝚺₁ trivially cannot contain K when 𝗜𝚺₁ ⪯ K), [𝗜𝚺₁ ⪯ F] is an unnecessary weakening relative to the source.

Def9 K F phrases local reflection using the standard provability predicate of a single (noncomputably chosen) Craig-trick Δ₁ reaxiomatization F.craig rather than quantifying over arbitrary algorithms or presentations enumerating F; due to intensionality of provability predicates, local reflection for another presentation of F does not automatically reduce to Def9 K F without K knowing their equivalence.

Target requires only that K extend 𝗜𝚺₁, be deductively closed (Def11 K), and be consistent (Def4 K), rather than full PA and factivity/truth as in EA; this is a harmless strengthening of the theorem relative to the source.

judgement.summary: Target faithfully captures the plain-arithmetic counterpart of Koellner's conditional (with the pointwise local reflection antecedent) and yields Penrose's conclusion as an immediate corollary, deriving both halves of F.theory ⊂ K without assuming them. The only divergences are minor formalization idealizations and scope choices: the absence of an object-language knowledge operator and truth predicate, the extra hypothesis 𝗜𝚺₁ ⪯ F, the use of a single Craig-trick presentation F.craig for local reflection, and the harmlessly weaker hypotheses on K.
